rationale: This is a level-to-trend substitution on an already-tested successful signal ("Noncash-Asset-Turnover Earnings Value"), and the archive's parallel experiment (level-based cash-share vs. "Rising-Liquidity Earnings Value" trend) already showed that swapping a level conditioner for its 3-period TREND weakens both the slope and the alpha, so this is a cosmetic variant with a predictable outcome.

This is a mechanical leg swap of "Depreciation-Reserved Liability Coverage Value" (oancf/P replaced by ib/P) using two conditioners already in the archive, and given the high cross-sectional correlation between earnings yield and operating-cash-flow yield it is unlikely to be economically distinct from the existing result.

The expression adds a balance-sheet stock (working-capital overhang, typically an order of magnitude larger than annual income) to a flow (-ib) in raw dollars, so the composite will be dominated by the overhang term and will not actually price the "joint" loss-plus-accrual burden the hypothesis describes; it is also the third recombination of the same two ingredients already tested via MIN and MUL.

The reasoning openly reverses the original economic hypothesis to fit a statistically null prior result (fmb_tstat 0.247, ls_talpha 1.478), so this is sign-fitting to noise on an opaque, poorly interpretable cash-flow line item rather than a motivated mechanism.

The high-water-mark release is a genuinely distinct quantity from the previously tested low-water-mark overhang (they differ for mid-range NWC) and the reversal-catalyst framing is coherent and correctly signed, though it sits close to the well-known working-capital accrual anomaly interacted with value and should be judged against that benchmark.

This is the same leg swap in the opposite direction (ib/P replaced by oancf/P in the already-tested "Noncash-Asset-Turnover Earnings Value"), combining two archive components with no new economic content beyond checking robustness across two highly correlated value anchors.
